mainTopic: The disagreement between רבי עקיבא and רבי יוסי הגלילי over which prohibitions count as a לאו הניתק לעשה (a prohibition that, once broken, can be fixed by a positive command). Two explanations are offered: the case of נבילה, or the word ״תעזוב״ in the laws of לקט, שכחה and פאה.
overview: This amud has three sections. First, the גמרא finishes explaining where רבי עקיבא and רבי יוסי הגלילי disagree about a לאו הניתק לעשה. One view says the argument is about נבילה, while אביי says everyone agrees about נבילה and the argument is about the word ״תעזוב״ in the gifts to the poor. Next, a ברייתא gives the order of the כהן גדול's וידוי. רבי מאיר says עויתי, פשעתי, חטאתי, following the פסוקים of the שעיר המשתלח and of משה. חכמים say it should go from light to heavy: חטאתי, עויתי, פשעתי. They explain that משה's verse was a request to treat זדונות like שגגות, and רב rules like חכמים. A story about a חזן who followed רבי מאיר shows how the verse of משה could mislead people. Finally, a ברייתא proves that the word וכפר by the כהן גדול's פר means atonement through spoken וידוי, not through blood.

steps.title: The dispute is about the prohibition of נבילה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא names the case where רבי עקיבא and רבי יוסי הגלילי disagree: the prohibition against eating נבילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They disagree about the prohibition of eating an animal that died without proper slaughter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question of exactly where the two תנאים disagree. It points to one case: the לאו of נבילה. The next line will spell out each side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah says 'Do not eat any נבילה; give it to the stranger in your gates.' A positive command comes right after the prohibition. That raises the question of whether this counts as a לאו הניתק לעשה, a prohibition whose violation is 'fixed' by a positive command and so is not punished with lashes. The גמרא is saying the whole argument comes down to how to classify this one לאו.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal that died without a kosher slaughter
A prohibition that, once broken, is 'repaired' by a positive command

phrases.english: It is about the prohibition of an unslaughtered carcass that they disagree:
phrases.notes: Based on דברים 14:21: 'Do not eat any נבילה; give it to the stranger.'

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּלָאו דִּנְבֵילָה קָא מִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question (on the previous amud) about where exactly the two תנאים disagree.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In what practical case do רבי עקיבא and רבי יוסי הגלילי disagree?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They disagree about the לאו of נבילה.

steps.title: Each side's view on נבילה
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא holds that the נבילה prohibition is a full לאו. רבי יוסי הגלילי holds it is not a full לאו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא holds it is a full prohibition. רבי יוסי הגלילי holds it is not a full prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains the two positions on the prohibition of נבילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי עקיבא, 'give it to the stranger' does not repair anything. Once you have eaten the meat, you cannot give it away anymore. So it is a regular לאו that carries מלקות. For רבי יוסי הגלילי, the positive command written right after the prohibition makes it a לאו הניתק לעשה, which is not a 'full' לאו.

keyTerms.meaning: A full-fledged, standard prohibition (punishable by lashes)
Lashes, the usual punishment for breaking a full לאו

steps.confusionAlert: Note the repeated word in ״לָאו לָאו מְעַלְּיָא״. The first לאו means 'not' and the second means 'prohibition.' So it reads: 'it is NOT a full prohibition.'

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva holds:
It is a full-fledged prohibition.
phrases.notes: So it carries lashes and is not 'fixed' by the positive command.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei HaGelili holds:
It is not a full-fledged prohibition.
phrases.notes: First לאו = 'not'; second לאו = 'prohibition.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא סָבַר: לָאו מְעַלְּיָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the two sides of the נבילה dispute named in step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי עקיבא: נבילה is a full לאו. רבי יוסי הגלילי: it is not a full לאו, because the positive command that follows it repairs it.

steps.title: אביי: everyone agrees about נבילה; the dispute is about ״תעזוב״
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects the נבילה explanation. He says everyone agrees נבילה is a full לאו, and the real dispute is about the word ״תעזוב״ in the gifts to the poor.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Everyone agrees that the prohibition of a carcass is a full prohibition. Here, they disagree about the word 'you shall leave.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי offers a different explanation of the dispute. He moves it away from נבילה and onto the verse about leaving crops for the poor. The next line will explain each side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי agrees that 'give it to the stranger' cannot repair eating נבילה, so for him no one treats it as a לאו הניתק לעשה. Instead he points to the gifts to the poor: לקט, שכחה and פאה. There the Torah lists several prohibitions and then says ״תעזוב״, 'you shall leave them for the poor.' The argument is whether that ״תעזוב״ repairs the prohibitions.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You shall leave' (Vayikra 19:9–10, gifts for the poor)
And here (introducing where the real dispute is)
Gleanings, forgotten sheaves, and the corner of the field, all left for the poor

phrases.english: Abaye said:
That according to everyone, the prohibition of a carcass —
is a full-fledged prohibition,
and here, it is about 'you shall leave' that they disagree,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:9–10: after 'do not reap the corner, do not gather the gleanings,' the verse says 'leave them for the poor.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָאו דִּנְבֵילָה לָאו מְעַלְּיָא הָוֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the explanation from steps 1–2 with a different case for the dispute.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the claim that the dispute is about נבילה. The dispute between the תנאים itself still stands.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: 'Give it to the stranger' cannot repair eating נבילה, so everyone would agree it is a full לאו.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The dispute is about whether ״תעזוב״ turns the poor-gift prohibitions into a לאו הניתק לעשה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows what a positive command needs in order to make a prohibition 'repairable.' It must be something you can still do after you have broken the prohibition.

steps.title: ״תעזוב״: from the start, or now?
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא reads ״תעזוב״ as 'leave it from the outset.' רבי יוסי הגלילי reads it as 'leave it now,' even after you have harvested it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא holds that 'you shall leave' means from the outset. רבי יוסי הגלילי holds that it means now.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the two readings of ״תעזוב״ according to אביי. This completes אביי's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא: ״תעזוב״ just restates the original duty to leave the crops in the field. It does not repair anything once you have broken the prohibition, so it is a full לאו. רבי יוסי הגלילי: ״תעזוב״ means that even after you wrongly harvested, you must now give the produce to the poor. That positive command repairs the violation, so it is a לאו הניתק לעשה.

keyTerms.meaning: From the outset / from the start

steps.whatToRemember: Two explanations of the same dispute. (1) נבילה: is it a full לאו or not? (2) אביי: everyone agrees נבילה is a full לאו. The real question is whether ״תעזוב״ means 'leave it from the start' (רבי עקיבא, so a full לאו) or 'leave it now, after harvesting' (רבי יוסי הגלילי, so a לאו הניתק לעשה).

phrases.english: For Rabbi Akiva holds:
'You shall leave' means from the outset,
phrases.notes: It does not repair a violation, so the prohibition stays a full לאו.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei HaGelili holds:
It means now.
phrases.notes: Even after harvesting, you must give the produce to the poor. That is a repair, so it is a לאו הניתק לעשה.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא סָבַר: ״תַּעֲזוֹב״ מֵעִיקָּרָא מַשְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the two readings of ״תעזוב″ behind אביי's version of the dispute.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי עקיבא: ״תעזוב″ means from the start, so it is a full לאו. רבי יוסי הגלילי: ״תעזוב″ means now, after violating, so it is a לאו הניתק לעשה.

steps.title: רבי מאיר's order of confession
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the confession is עויתי, פשעתי, וחטאתי. It brings proof from the שעיר המשתלח and from משה. This is רבי מאיר's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: How does he confess? 'I did wrong, I rebelled, and I sinned.' The same order appears for the goat sent away: 'And he shall confess over it all the wrongdoings of the Jewish people, and all their rebellions, for all their sins.' The same order appears with משה: 'Forgiving wrongdoing and rebellion and sin.' These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: the exact words the כהן גדול says when he confesses on יום כפור. רבי מאיר says the order is עון, then פשע, then חטא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר does not just state the order. He shows it comes straight from the Torah. The same three words appear in this order in the פסוק about the שעיר המשתלח and in משה's description of how ה׳ forgives.

keyTerms.meaning: The goat sent away to עזאזל on יום כפור.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: How does he confess?
'I did wrong, I rebelled, and I sinned,'
and likewise, regarding the goat that is sent away, it says:

phrases.aramaic: ״וְהִתְוַדָּה עָלָיו אֶת כׇּל עֲוֹנוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
phrases.english: 'And he shall confess over it all the wrongdoings of the children of Israel'
'and all their rebellions, for all their sins,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא טז:כא

phrases.english: and likewise, regarding Moses, it says:
'Forgiving wrongdoing and rebellion and sin,'
phrases.notes: שמות לד:ז

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: כֵּיצַד מִתְוַדֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: the wording of the וידוי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, the confession order is עויתי, פשעתי, חטאתי, based on the order of the words in the פסוקים.

steps.title: The Sages define the three kinds of sin
steps.stepSummary: חכמים explain each word. עונות are deliberate sins, פשעים are rebellious sins, and חטאים are accidental sins. Each definition is proven from a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: חכמים say: 'עונות' are deliberate sins, as it says, 'That soul shall surely be cut off, its sin is upon it.' 'פשעים' are acts of rebellion, as it says, 'The king of Moab rebelled against me,' and also, 'Then Livnah rebelled at that time.' 'All their sins (חטאתם)' are accidental sins, as it says, 'A soul that sins by accident.'
steps.whatsHappening: חכמים begin their response by defining what each of the three words means. This sets up their challenge to רבי מאיר's order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word gets a proof. עון appears with כרת, which is a punishment only for deliberate sin. פשע appears where kings rebel against their rulers. חטא appears in the פסוק about a person who sins בשגגה, by accident. So the three words go from medium, to most severe, to least severe.

keyTerms.meaning: Sins of rebellion, done to defy ה׳.
'Shall surely be cut off' (כרת). This punishment applies only to deliberate sins.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up 'חטא' as a general word for any sin with its narrow meaning here. In this list it specifically means an accidental sin.

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
'wrongdoings' are the deliberate sins,
and so it says:
'That soul shall surely be cut off; its wrongdoing is upon it.'
phrases.notes: במדבר טו:לא

phrases.english: 'Rebellions' are the acts of defiance,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן הוּא אוֹמֵר: ״מֶלֶךְ מוֹאָב פָּשַׁע בִּי״,
phrases.english: and so it says: 'The king of Moab rebelled against me,'
phrases.notes: מלכים ב ג:ז

phrases.english: and it says: 'Then Livnah rebelled at that time.'
phrases.notes: מלכים ב ח:כב

phrases.english: 'For all their sins' refers to the accidental sins,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן הוּא אוֹמֵר: ״נֶפֶשׁ כִּי תֶחֱטָא בִשְׁגָגָה״.
phrases.english: and so it says: 'A soul that sins accidentally.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא ד:ב

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: עֲוֹנוֹת אֵלּוּ הַזְּדוֹנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: חכמים respond to רבי מאיר by first defining his three terms.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עון means זדון, פשע means מרד, and חטא means שגגה.

steps.title: You don't go back to small sins after confessing big ones
steps.stepSummary: חכמים ask: after confessing deliberate and rebellious sins, would he then go back and confess accidental ones?
steps.simpleTranslation: And after he has already confessed the deliberate sins and the rebellious sins, does he go back and confess the accidental sins?!
steps.whatsHappening: Using their definitions, חכמים attack רבי מאיר's order as illogical.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The heavier sins already include the lighter ones. If someone has asked forgiveness for the worst sins, it makes no sense to go back down to the smallest. A proper confession should build up from light to heavy.

phrases.aramaic: וּמֵאַחַר שֶׁהִתְוַדָּה עַל הַזְּדוֹנוֹת וְעַל הַמְּרָדִים
phrases.english: And once he has confessed the deliberate sins and the rebellious sins,
does he then go back and confess the accidental sins?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמֵאַחַר שֶׁהִתְוַדָּה עַל הַזְּדוֹנוֹת וְעַל הַמְּרָדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the definitions from step 6 to attack the order from step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's order: עויתי, פשעתי, חטאתי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Confession should rise from light to severe. Ending with the lightest sin after the heavy ones is backwards.

steps.title: The Sages' correct order: חטאתי, עויתי, פשעתי
steps.stepSummary: חכמים give the proper order: I sinned by accident, I did wrong on purpose, I rebelled.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is how he would confess: 'I have sinned, I have done wrong, and I have rebelled before You, I and my household,' and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: Having rejected רבי מאיר's order, חכמים now state the order they hold is correct.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new order goes from light to heavy. First comes שגגה, then זדון, then מרד. This fixes the problem raised in step 7.

keyTerms.meaning: I and my household (the כהן גדול's family).

phrases.english: Rather, this is how he would confess:
I have sinned, and I have done wrong, and I have rebelled before You,
I and my household, etc.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא כָּךְ הָיָה מִתְוַדֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers the replacement order after the challenge in step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replaces the challenged wording with a logical light-to-heavy order.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The confession follows the order of the פסוק about the שעיר: עון, פשע, חטא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The confession goes חטאתי, עויתי, פשעתי.

steps.title: Support from דוד, שלמה, and דניאל
steps.stepSummary: חכמים show that the confessions of דוד, שלמה, and דניאל all begin with חטאנו, the accidental sins.
steps.simpleTranslation: And likewise, regarding דוד it says: 'We have sinned with our fathers, we have done wrong, we have acted wickedly.' And likewise, regarding שלמה it says: 'We have sinned (and acted wickedly and rebelled).' And likewise, regarding דניאל it says: 'We have sinned (and done wrong), and acted wickedly, and rebelled.'
steps.whatsHappening: חכמים bring three פסוקים where great people confessed in the light-to-heavy order, to back up their view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of these real confessions opens with חטאנו, the lightest sin, and moves to heavier words. This answers רבי מאיר's proofs with proofs of their own, taken from actual prayers of confession.

phrases.english: And likewise, regarding David it says:
'We have sinned with our fathers, we have done wrong, we have acted wickedly,'
phrases.notes: תהלים קו:ו

phrases.english: and likewise, regarding Solomon it says:
'We have sinned (and acted wickedly and rebelled),'
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets. The quote is from the פסוק in מלכים א ח:מז.

phrases.english: and likewise, regarding Daniel it says:
'We have sinned (and done wrong), and acted wickedly, and rebelled.'
phrases.notes: דניאל ט:ה

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן בְּדָוִד הוּא אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the order given in step 8.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The confessions of דוד (תהלים), שלמה (מלכים), and דניאל.

steps.title: But what about משה's verse?
steps.stepSummary: חכמים must explain why משה said עון, פשע, חטאה, in רבי מאיר's order.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then what about what משה said: 'Forgiving wrongdoing and rebellion and sin'?
steps.whatsHappening: חכמים raise the strongest point against their own view: משה's verse lists the sins in רבי מאיר's order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verses about the שעיר and about משה seem to support רבי מאיר. חכמים need to explain why משה put חטאה, the lightest sin, last.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What is (the meaning of) what he said?'

phrases.english: But then what is it that Moses said:
'Forgiving wrongdoing and rebellion and sin'?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מַהוּ שֶׁאָמַר מֹשֶׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges חכמים' order from step 8, using רבי מאיר's proof from step 5.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: משה's verse ends with the lightest sin, matching רבי מאיר.

steps.title: משה asked that deliberate sins be treated as accidental
steps.stepSummary: משה's verse is not a confession order. It is a request that when ישראל do תשובה, their זדונות be treated like שגגות.
steps.simpleTranslation: משה said before ה׳: Master of the World, when ישראל sin before You and do תשובה, make their deliberate sins like accidental sins.
steps.whatsHappening: חכמים answer the challenge by explaining that משה's words have a different purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה was not listing a confession order. He was praying. 'Forgive עון and פשע as if they were חטאה' means treat the heavy sins as light ones. So חטאה comes last because it is the goal of the request, not the third item in a list.

keyTerms.meaning: Deliberate sins treated as accidental ones.

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a key idea about תשובה: through repentance, sins done on purpose can be treated like sins done by mistake.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר מֹשֶׁה לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא:
phrases.english: Moses said before the Holy One, Blessed be He:
Master of the World,
when Israel sins before You
and repents,
make their deliberate sins like accidental sins.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מֹשֶׁה לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the verse: it is a request, not an order of confession.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: משה's verse gives the order of confession, as רבי מאיר says.
steps.terutzMaskana: משה asked that עון and פשע be treated like חטאה (שגגה) once ישראל do תשובה.

steps.title: The הלכה follows חכמים
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר שמואל, in the name of רב, rules like חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר שמואל said in the name of רב: The הלכה follows the words of חכמים.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא gives the practical ruling in the dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In practice, the confession is said חטאתי, עויתי, פשעתי, from light to heavy.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rabba bar Shmuel said in the name of Rav:
The halacha follows the words of the Sages.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the dispute between steps 5 and 8.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The confession is חטאתי, עויתי, פשעתי.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב needed to say this, since the majority always wins against one opinion.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious! When it is one person against many, the הלכה follows the many.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions why רב's ruling was needed at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a general rule: יחיד ורבים, הלכה כרבים. When one Sage argues against a group, the הלכה follows the group. Since רבי מאיר is alone against חכמים, the ruling seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is obvious!' This questions why a statement was needed.

phrases.english: It is obvious: when it is an individual against the many, the halacha follows the many!

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּשִׁיטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for רב's ruling in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that the הלכה follows חכמים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The general majority rule already decides this, so the ruling adds nothing.

steps.title: משה's verse might have tipped the scales
steps.stepSummary: Without רב's ruling, we might have followed רבי מאיר because משה's verse supports him. רב teaches that we do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said that רבי מאיר's reasoning makes sense, because the verse about משה supports him. So רב teaches us that the הלכה still follows חכמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רב's ruling was necessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sometimes a lone opinion can win if it has strong support. משה's verse matches רבי מאיר's order, so one might think he wins here despite being alone. רב tells us the majority rule still applies, especially since חכמים explained the verse differently.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You might have said.' This introduces a mistaken assumption.

steps.whatToRemember: The וידוי goes from light to heavy: חטאתי (accidental), עויתי (deliberate), פשעתי (rebellious). The הלכה follows חכמים even though משה's verse seemed to support רבי מאיר, because that verse is a request to treat זדונות כשגגות.

phrases.english: You might have said
that Rabbi Meir's reasoning is convincing,
since the verse of Moses supports him,
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא challenge from step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: explains a mistaken assumption the ruling comes to prevent.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: משה's verse might make רבי מאיר win even though he is alone.
steps.terutzMaskana: The הלכה follows חכמים despite the support from משה's verse.

steps.title: רבה challenges a prayer leader who followed רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: A חזן led the תפילה before רבה and confessed in רבי מאיר's order. רבה challenged him for leaving the majority view of the חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man went down to lead the prayers before רבה, and he did the confession like רבי מאיר. רבה said to him: You left the רבנן and acted like רבי מאיר?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that tests the ruling of רב from the previous steps. A חזן used רבי מאיר's order of confession, and רבה objects.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ruled like חכמים: חטאים (accidental) first, then עונות (deliberate), then פשעים (rebellious). רבה expects everyone to follow that ruling, so he is surprised that this חזן used רבי מאיר's order, עונות, פשעים, חטאים, instead.

keyTerms.meaning: Went down before him, meaning he led the prayers as חזן (in the old days the חזן stood in a lower spot)

phrases.english: A certain man who went down to lead prayers before Rabba
and he did the confession like Rabbi Meir,
Rabba said to him:
You left the Rabbis
phrases.notes: The רבנן are the majority.

phrases.english: and acted like Rabbi Meir?!

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁבְקַתְּ רַבָּנַן וְעָבְדַתְּ כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story that applies רב's ruling (step 12) and the worry from step 14 that people might follow רבי מאיר because of משה's verse.
steps.kashyaTarget: The חזן's choice to confess in רבי מאיר's order
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The הלכה follows the majority, the חכמים, as רב ruled. So why act like a single opinion?

steps.title: The prayer leader defends himself with משה's verse
steps.stepSummary: The חזן answers that he holds like רבי מאיר, because that order is written in the תורה of משה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I hold like רבי מאיר, as it is written in the book of the תורה of משה.
steps.whatsHappening: The חזן explains his choice. He relies on the verse משה said: עון, פשע, חטאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is exactly the mistake step 14 warned about. The verse seems to support רבי מאיר, but step 11 already explained that משה was not giving a confession order. He was asking that זדונות be treated like שגגות. That is why רב had to rule like חכמים.

keyTerms.meaning: I hold / that is my opinion

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the חזן's answer wins. The גמרא already answered his proof in step 11, and רב ruled like חכמים. The story shows how a person might get confused, and it does not change the הלכה.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: Now the speaker is the חזן.

phrases.english: I hold like Rabbi Meir,
as it is written in the book of the Torah of Moses.
phrases.notes: This refers to the verse נשא עון ופשע וחטאה.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר סְבִירָא לִי, כְּדִכְתִיב בְּסֵפֶר אוֹרָיְיתָא דְּמֹשֶׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The חזן responds to רבה's challenge.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Following a single opinion against the majority is wrong.
steps.terutzMaskana: The חזן feels a clear verse in the Torah justifies following רבי מאיר. The גמרא's earlier answer (step 11) shows this reading is not accepted.

steps.title: A ברייתא: the word 'atone' refers to atonement through words
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא teaches that the word וכפר said about the כהן גדול's פר means atonement through spoken וידוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: 'And he shall atone.' The verse is speaking about atonement through words.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic with a ברייתא. It explains what the word וכפר means in the פר section of יום הכיפורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse says the כהן גדול brings his פר 'and atones for himself and his household.' The ברייתא claims this כפרה is done by speaking the וידוי, not by an action with the animal.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: "And he shall atone"
phrases.notes: From ויקרא טז:ו, about the פר.

phrases.english: the verse is speaking about atonement through words.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: וְכִפֶּר, בְּכַפָּרַת דְּבָרִים הַכָּתוּב מְדַבֵּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new ברייתא about the source for וידוי on the פר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The וכפר of the פר refers to atonement through spoken וידוי.

steps.title: Maybe 'atone' means atonement through blood
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks: maybe וכפר means the atonement of sprinkling blood, as with other קרבנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: You say it means atonement through words. Or perhaps it only means atonement through blood?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא questions its own claim. It is setting up the proofs that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With most קרבנות, the word כפרה refers to sprinkling the blood on the מזבח. So it is reasonable to think the וכפר here also means the blood, not the וידוי.

keyTerms.meaning: You say (opens a question about a derivation)

phrases.english: You say it is atonement through words,
or perhaps it is only atonement through blood.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתָּה אוֹמֵר בְּכַפָּרַת דְּבָרִים, אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא כַּפָּרַת דָּמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the claim of step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does וכפר refer to atonement through words or through blood?

steps.title: Proof by comparison to the scapegoat
steps.stepSummary: The word כפרה appears both by the שעיר המשתלח and by the פר. Since the שעיר's כפרה can only be through words, the פר's כפרה is also through words.
steps.simpleTranslation: I will learn it this way: 'atonement' is said here, and 'atonement' is said there. Just as the atonement said by the שעיר is through words, so too the atonement said by the פר is through words.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא proves its point by comparing two verses that use the same word, כפרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שעיר המשתלח is not slaughtered, and its blood is never sprinkled. So its כפרה must come through the וידוי said over it. The shared word teaches that the פר's כפרה works the same way.

keyTerms.meaning: I will derive it by reasoning
Here... there (the two places being compared)
The goat, here the שעיר המשתלח (scapegoat)
The bull of the כהן גדול

phrases.english: I will reason it out:
"Atonement" is said here,
phrases.notes: Here means by the פר.

phrases.english: and "atonement" is said there.
phrases.notes: There means by the שעיר המשתלח, ויקרא טז:י.

phrases.english: Just as the atonement said by the goat is through words,
so too the atonement said by the bull is through words.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲרֵי אֲנִי דָּן: נֶאֶמְרָה כָּאן כַּפָּרָה, וְנֶאֶמְרָה לְהַלָּן כַּפָּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18 with a first proof.
steps.raayaObject: The וכפר of the פר means atonement through words.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The שעיר המשתלח, whose כפרה must be through words since it has no slaughter or blood sprinkling.

steps.title: Second proof: 'atone' comes before the bull is slaughtered
steps.stepSummary: The verse says וכפר before the פר is slaughtered, so the כפרה cannot be the blood. It must be the וידוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want to argue, look: the verse says 'And אהרן shall bring near his own bull of the חטאת and atone for himself and for his household,' and the bull has not yet been slaughtered.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a backup proof in case someone rejects the first one. It points to the order of the verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood is only available after slaughter. The Torah mentions כפרה while the פר is still alive, and the slaughter is only mentioned afterward. So the כפרה here must be through words.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish to argue (introduces a second, stronger proof)
And it has not yet been slaughtered

steps.whatToRemember: The וכפר of the כהן גדול's פר means וידוי, not blood. There are two proofs: the comparison to the שעיר המשתלח, and the fact that the verse says וכפר before the פר is slaughtered.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the Torah source for the כהן גדול's וידוי over his פר, which the משנה described earlier.

phrases.english: And if you wish to argue:
look, the verse says:

phrases.aramaic: ״וְהִקְרִיב אַהֲרֹן אֶת פַּר הַחַטָּאת אֲשֶׁר לוֹ
phrases.english: "And Aaron shall bring near his own bull of the sin-offering
and atone for himself and for his household,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא טז:יא. The slaughter is only mentioned after this.

phrases.english: and the bull has not yet been slaughtered.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם נַפְשְׁךָ לוֹמַר: הֲרֵי הוּא אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, independent proof in case the comparison in step 19 is rejected.
steps.raayaObject: The וכפר of the פר means atonement through words.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא טז:יא, where וכפר comes before the slaughter of the פר.

steps.title: Why did the ברייתא need a second proof?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the ברייתא meant by 'ואם נפשך לומר'. Why was the first proof not enough?
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'and if you wish to say' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask about the ברייתא's wording. It is setting up the next step, which will explain what was weak about the first proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'ואם נפשך לומר' usually means 'even if you can push back on the first argument, here is another one.' So the גמרא wants to know how someone could push back on the comparison to the שעיר המשתלח from Step 19.

keyTerms.meaning: What is / what does it mean
And if you wish to say. It introduces a backup argument for when the first one can be questioned.

phrases.english: What is the meaning of 'and if you wish to say'?
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quoting the ברייתא's own wording, which led into the second proof in Step 20.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי ״וְאִם נַפְשְׁךָ לוֹמַר״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks why the ברייתא added the second proof (Step 20) after the first proof (Step 19).
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What weakness in the first proof (comparing to the שעיר המשתלח) made the second proof necessary?

steps.title: The first comparison could have pointed to the inner goat instead
steps.stepSummary: Someone might compare the פר to the שעיר that is offered inside, whose כפרה comes through blood. So the ברייתא brought the second proof: וכפר is written before the פר is slaughtered.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say, let us learn from the goat offered inside, whose atonement is through blood. That is why the verse says 'and he shall atone,' and the bull has not yet been slaughtered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. The first proof was weak because a different goat could be used for the comparison. That is why the ברייתא needed the second proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first proof compared the פר to the שעיר המשתלח, whose כפרה is only through words. But there is another שעיר on יום כיפור, the inner one, whose blood is sprinkled inside, so its כפרה is through blood. Since we cannot be sure which goat to compare to, the ברייתא relies on the order of the verse: וכפר comes before the slaughter, so it cannot mean the blood.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you say. It introduces a possible objection.
The goat offered inside, whose blood is sprinkled in the קודש הקדשים

steps.whatToRemember: A comparison through a shared word can fail when there are two possible sources to compare to. A proof from the order of the verse settles it: the פר's כפרה is the וידוי.
steps.confusionAlert: There are two goats on יום כיפור. The שעיר המשתלח (sent away, no blood offered) and the inner שעיר (its blood is sprinkled inside). Don't mix them up.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows why the ברייתא's second proof is the decisive one. The word וכפר before the slaughter cannot mean the blood.

phrases.english: And if you say, let us derive
from the goat that is offered inside,
phrases.notes: This is the inner goat, not the שעיר המשתלח.

phrases.english: whose atonement is through blood,
therefore it says 'and he shall atone,'
and the bull has not yet been slaughtered.
phrases.notes: No blood exists yet, so the כפרה must be through words (וידוי).

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא נֵילַף מִשָּׂעִיר הַנַּעֲשֶׂה בִּפְנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 21 by naming the weakness in the first proof.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The first proof could be challenged by comparing the פר to the inner שעיר, whose כפרה is through blood. So the ברייתא added the proof from the verse's order: וכפר comes before the פר is slaughtered.
